mechanism_narrative: The sustained increase in WORKPLACES mobility over the past two weeks indicates a gradual return to office-based work, which will directly increase foot traffic in nearby retail and recreation establishments, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rebound in PARKS mobility from its lowest point suggests increased public comfort with outdoor activities. This comfort will translate into greater willingness to visit other public spaces, including retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility rises by more than 10 percentage points week-on-week from its lowest point in the last 4 weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility rises by more than 10 points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent two weeks, the hypothesis is falsified.

failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility show an upward trend, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase relative to the last 28 days, this hypothesis is falsified.
